candidates.phrase: most just, and terrible in his judgments
candidates.rationale: Directly predicates 'most just' of the one true God as an essential attribute.
candidates.chunk_text: There is but one only, living, and true God, who is infinite in being and perfection, a most pure spirit, invisible, without body, parts, or passions; immutable, immense, eternal, incomprehensible, almighty, most wise, most holy, most free, most absolute; working all things according to the counsel of his own immutable and most righteous will, for his own glory; most loving, gracious, merciful, long-suffering, abundant in goodness and truth, forgiving iniquity, transgression, and sin; the rewarder of them that diligently seek him; and withal, most just, and terrible in his judgments, hating all sin, and who will by no means clear the guilty.

candidates.phrase: being most holy and righteous, neither is nor can be the author
candidates.rationale: Asserts God himself is 'most righteous' in his nature, excluding him from authorship of sin.
candidates.chunk_text: The almighty power, unsearchable wisdom, and infinite goodness of God so far manifest themselves in his providence, that it extendeth itself even to the first fall, and all other sins of angels and men; and that not by a bare permission, but such as hath joined with it a most wise and powerful bounding, and otherwise ordering, and governing of them, in a manifold dispensation, to his own holy ends; yet so, as the sinfulness thereof proceedeth only from the creature, and not from God, who, being most holy and righteous, neither is nor can be the author or approver of sin.

candidates.phrase: to the praise of the glory of his wisdom, power, justice, goodness, and mercy
candidates.rationale: Lists justice among God's own perfections displayed in his providential governance, affirming his justice as an attribute.
candidates.chunk_text: God the great Creator of all things doth uphold, direct, dispose, and govern all creatures, actions, and things, from the greatest even to the least, by his most wise and holy providence, according to his infallible foreknowledge, and the free and immutable counsel of his own will, to the praise of the glory of his wisdom, power, justice, goodness, and mercy.

candidates.phrase: most holy, most just, most merciful and gracious
candidates.rationale: Directly attributes the perfection of justice to God as one of His essential attributes.
candidates.chunk_text: What is God? A. God is a Spirit, in and of himself infinite in being, glory, blessedness, and perfection; all-sufficient, eternal, unchangeable, incomprehensible, everywhere present, almighty, knowing all things, most wise, most holy, most just, most merciful and gracious, longsuffering, and abundant in goodness and truth.

candidates.phrase: employing them all, at his pleasure, in the administrations of his power, mercy, and justice
candidates.rationale: Names justice as an attribute God exercises in His providential administration, affirming His righteous character.
candidates.chunk_text: What is God’s providence towards the angels? A. God by his providence permitted some of the angels, willfully and irrecoverably, to fall into sin and damnation, limiting and ordering that, and all their sins, to his own glory; and established the rest in holiness and happiness; employing them all, at his pleasure, in the administrations of his power, mercy, and justice.

candidates.phrase: to satisfy God’s justice, procure his favor
candidates.rationale: Presupposes and affirms God's justice as a real divine attribute that must be satisfied, implying His righteousness.
candidates.chunk_text: Why was it requisite that the mediator should be God? A. It was requisite that the mediator should be God, that he might sustain and keep the human nature from sinking under the infinite wrath of God, and the power of death; give worth and efficacy to his sufferings, obedience, and intercession; and to satisfy God’s justice, procure his favor, purchase a peculiar people, give his Spirit to them, conquer all their enemies, and bring them to everlasting salvation.

candidates.phrase: omnipotent and supremely wise, kind and merciful, just and true
candidates.rationale: Directly predicates 'just' of the one God's essence and nature in the confession's own summary statement.
candidates.chunk_text: GOD IS ONE. We believe and teach that God is one in essence or nature, subsisting in himself, all sufficient in himself, invisible, incorporeal, immense, eternal, Creator of all things both visible and invisible, the greatest good, living, quickening and preserving all things, omnipotent and supremely wise, kind and merciful, just and true. Truly we detest many gods because it is expressly written: “The Lord your God is one Lord” (Deut. 6:4). “I am the Lord your God. You shall have no other gods before me” (Ex. 20:2–3). “I am the Lord, and there is no other god besides me. Am I not the Lord, and there is no other God beside me? A righteous God and a Savior; there is none besides me” (Isa. 45:, 21). “The Lord, the Lord, a God merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love and faithfulness” (Ex. 34:6).

candidates.phrase: God is certainly merciful, but also just
candidates.rationale: Directly predicates justice of God alongside mercy, affirming perfect divine justice.
candidates.chunk_text: Q. But isn’t God also merciful? A. God is certainly merciful, but also just. God’s justice demands that sin, committed against his supreme majesty, be punished with the supreme penalty— eternal punishment of body and soul.

candidates.phrase: As a just judge, God will punish them
candidates.rationale: Asserts God acts as a just judge, affirming divine righteousness in judgment.
candidates.chunk_text: Q. Does God permit such disobedience and rebellion to go unpunished? A. Certainly not. God is terribly angry with the sin we are born with as well as the sins we personally commit. As a just judge, God will punish them both now and in eternity, having declared: “Cursed is everyone who does not observe and obey all the things written in the book of the law.”

candidates.phrase: According to God's righteous judgment we deserve punishment
candidates.rationale: Describes God's judgment as righteous, affirming God's justice narrowly in context of judgment.
candidates.chunk_text: Q. According to God’s righteous judgment we deserve punishment both now and in eternity: how then can we escape this punishment and return to God’s favor? A. God requires that his justice be satisfied. Therefore the claims of this justice must be paid in full, either by ourselves or by another.

candidates.phrase: completely wise, just, and good
candidates.rationale: Directly attributes justice as an essential attribute of the one God, satisfying the shared divine justice floor.
candidates.chunk_text: We all believe in our hearts and confess with our mouths that there is a single and simple spiritual being, whom we call God— eternal, incomprehensible, invisible, unchangeable, infinite, almighty; completely wise, just, and good, and the overflowing source of all good.

candidates.locator: Article 20: The Justice and Mercy of God in Christ
candidates.phrase: who is perfectly merciful and also very just
candidates.rationale: Asserts God himself is 'very just' as a perfect divine attribute, meeting the floor for God's justice.
candidates.chunk_text: We believe that God— who is perfectly merciful and also very just— sent the Son to assume the nature in which the disobedience had been committed, in order to bear in it the punishment of sin by his most bitter passion and death. So God made known his justice toward his Son, who was charged with our sin, and he poured out his goodness and mercy on us, who are guilty and worthy of damnation, giving to us his Son to die, by a most perfect love, and raising him to life for our justification, in order that by him we might have immortality and eternal life.

candidates.phrase: God showed himself to be as he is: merciful and just
candidates.rationale: States God's essential character includes being just, directly predicating justice of God.
candidates.chunk_text: We believe that— all Adam’s descendants having thus fallen into perdition and ruin by the sin of Adam— God showed himself to be as he is: merciful and just. God is merciful in withdrawing and saving from this perdition those who, in the eternal and unchangeable divine counsel, have been elected and chosen in Jesus Christ our Lord by his pure goodness, without any consideration of their works. God is just in leaving the others in their ruin and fall into which they plunged themselves.

survivors.locator: Chapter 2.1 — Of God, and of the Holy Trinity
survivors.phrase: most just, and terrible in his judgments
survivors.rationale: Directly predicates 'most just' of the one true God as an essential attribute.
survivors.chunk_text: There is but one only, living, and true God, who is infinite in being and perfection, a most pure spirit, invisible, without body, parts, or passions; immutable, immense, eternal, incomprehensible, almighty, most wise, most holy, most free, most absolute; working all things according to the counsel of his own immutable and most righteous will, for his own glory; most loving, gracious, merciful, long-suffering, abundant in goodness and truth, forgiving iniquity, transgression, and sin; the rewarder of them that diligently seek him; and withal, most just, and terrible in his judgments, hating all sin, and who will by no means clear the guilty.

survivors.phrase: in his being, wisdom, power, holiness, justice, goodness and truth
survivors.rationale: Defines God's essential attributes, explicitly including justice as belonging to God himself.
survivors.chunk_text: What is God? A. God is a spirit, infinite, eternal, and unchangeable, in his being, wisdom, power, holiness, justice, goodness and truth.

survivors.phrase: most holy, most just, most merciful and gracious
survivors.rationale: Directly attributes the perfection of justice to God as one of His essential attributes.
survivors.chunk_text: What is God? A. God is a Spirit, in and of himself infinite in being, glory, blessedness, and perfection; all-sufficient, eternal, unchangeable, incomprehensible, everywhere present, almighty, knowing all things, most wise, most holy, most just, most merciful and gracious, longsuffering, and abundant in goodness and truth.

survivors.phrase: omnipotent and supremely wise, kind and merciful, just and true
survivors.rationale: Directly predicates 'just' of the one God's essence and nature in the confession's own summary statement.
survivors.chunk_text: GOD IS ONE. We believe and teach that God is one in essence or nature, subsisting in himself, all sufficient in himself, invisible, incorporeal, immense, eternal, Creator of all things both visible and invisible, the greatest good, living, quickening and preserving all things, omnipotent and supremely wise, kind and merciful, just and true. Truly we detest many gods because it is expressly written: “The Lord your God is one Lord” (Deut. 6:4). “I am the Lord your God. You shall have no other gods before me” (Ex. 20:2–3). “I am the Lord, and there is no other god besides me. Am I not the Lord, and there is no other God beside me? A righteous God and a Savior; there is none besides me” (Isa. 45:, 21). “The Lord, the Lord, a God merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love and faithfulness” (Ex. 34:6).

survivors.phrase: God is certainly merciful, but also just
survivors.rationale: Directly predicates justice of God alongside mercy, affirming perfect divine justice.
survivors.chunk_text: Q. But isn’t God also merciful? A. God is certainly merciful, but also just. God’s justice demands that sin, committed against his supreme majesty, be punished with the supreme penalty— eternal punishment of body and soul.

survivors.rationale: Directly attributes justice as an essential attribute of the one God, satisfying the shared divine justice floor.
survivors.chunk_text: We all believe in our hearts and confess with our mouths that there is a single and simple spiritual being, whom we call God— eternal, incomprehensible, invisible, unchangeable, infinite, almighty; completely wise, just, and good, and the overflowing source of all good.

survivors.phrase: being most holy and righteous, neither is nor can be the author
survivors.rationale: Asserts God himself is 'most righteous' in his nature, excluding him from authorship of sin.
survivors.chunk_text: The almighty power, unsearchable wisdom, and infinite goodness of God so far manifest themselves in his providence, that it extendeth itself even to the first fall, and all other sins of angels and men; and that not by a bare permission, but such as hath joined with it a most wise and powerful bounding, and otherwise ordering, and governing of them, in a manifold dispensation, to his own holy ends; yet so, as the sinfulness thereof proceedeth only from the creature, and not from God, who, being most holy and righteous, neither is nor can be the author or approver of sin.

survivors.phrase: As a just judge, God will punish them
survivors.rationale: Asserts God acts as a just judge, affirming divine righteousness in judgment.
survivors.chunk_text: Q. Does God permit such disobedience and rebellion to go unpunished? A. Certainly not.
